text.p: Beverly Enterprises Inc and Capstone Pharmacy Services Inc said Wednesday they had signed a definitive agreement to combine Beverly's Pharmacy Corp of America unit with Capstone to create the largest independent U.S. institutional pharmacy company.
In the deal, Capstone said it will issue about 50 million shares of its stock to Beverly shareholders and assume $275 million of debt.
Capstone said the 50 million shares are worth $587.5 million, based on its April 15 closing price of 11-3/4.
The transaction will be accretive to Capstone, increasing annual earnings per share by at least 10 percent, the companies said.
After the transaction, Capstone will have revenues totalling about $900 million, some 30 percent higher than its nearest competitor, they said.
The combined company will serve the pharmaceutical and medical needs of nearly 500,000 customers, and operate some 100 institutional pharmacies in 32 states, the companies said.

Beverly shareholders will receive about 0.44 share of Capstone for each share of Beverly, and cumulatively will own about 57 percent of the combined pharmacy company. Beverly Enterprises will not retain any ownership position.

C. Arnold Renschler will serve as president and chief executive officer of Capstone, the companies said. Currently he is president of Beverly's Pharmacy Corp of America and executive vice president of Beverly.
